title: Gears grinding or stripped
summary: You hear grinding or clicking, or the motor spins but the car doesn't move.
words: grinding clicking stripped gear gears teeth broken noise crunching motor spins car not moving no drive pinion spur mesh slipper clutch
causes: The gear mesh (how tightly the teeth of the two gears sit together) is too tight or too loose.
The motor screws have come loose, so the motor moves away from the gear.
The slipper clutch (a part that lets the gears slip a little to protect them from hard hits) is tightened all the way.
Landing jumps with the throttle on, or small stones getting into the gears.
steps: Unplug the battery and take off the gear cover.
Look at the teeth on the pinion (the small metal gear on the motor) and the spur gear (the big gear it drives). Missing or melted teeth mean the gear needs replacing.
Loosen the motor screws just enough for the motor to slide.
Put a strip of normal paper between the two gears, push the motor in so the paper is squeezed between the teeth, and tighten the motor screws.
Turn the gears to roll the paper out. It should come out with tooth marks but not torn.
Hold the spur gear still and gently rock the pinion. You should feel a tiny click of play. No play at all means too tight; a clear wobble means too loose.
Turn the spur gear a quarter turn and check again, all the way round. Spur gears are rarely perfectly round, so set the mesh at the tightest spot.
If your car has a slipper clutch, don't tighten it fully. Tighten it, then loosen it about half a turn.
warn: Never mix gear pitches (the size of the teeth), even if two gears look the same. A 32P gear will not work with a Mod 0.8 or 48P gear, and both will strip.
tip: Put a small drop of threadlock (a screw glue that can still be undone later) on the grub screw (the tiny screw that holds the pinion on the motor shaft).
faq: Why does my RC car keep stripping spur gears?

Almost always gear mesh. Too tight and the teeth overheat and melt; too loose and the pinion skips over the tips and shears them. A loose motor mount, a fully locked slipper clutch or landing jumps on throttle make it worse.
Metal or plastic spur gear: which is better?

On 2S–3S 1/10 cars a plastic spur is fine and acts as a cheap fuse: it strips before more expensive diff gears do. Hardened steel spurs make sense on heavy 4S–6S trucks and high-torque brushless crawlers, as long as the mesh is set accurately.
How do I check gear mesh without a tool?
Use the paper method: a strip of normal paper between pinion and spur, push them together, tighten the motor and roll the paper out. Light tooth marks without tearing means the mesh is right.
Can I use a 32P pinion with a Mod 0.8 spur?
No. They look almost identical but the tooth shapes differ, and mixing them strips both gears quickly. Always match the pitch printed on the spur gear.
cause: Usually the gear mesh is too tight or too loose, or the slipper clutch is locked fully.
quick: Check the pinion and spur for missing or melted teeth, and replace damaged gears.
Reset the mesh with the paper-strip test: light tooth marks, no tearing.
Back the slipper clutch off about half a turn from fully tight.
Never mix gear pitches (32P, 48P, Mod 0.8), even if they look the same.

title: Bottoming out or bouncy suspension
summary: The chassis slams the ground on jumps, the car bounces a lot, or a shock leaks oil.
words: bottoming out bottom hits ground jumps landing bouncy bounce suspension too soft shocks leaking oil leak shock absorber damper spring sag
causes: The shock oil (the oil inside each shock that slows its movement) is too thin. Heat makes it even thinner, so this is worse in summer.
The springs are too soft for the weight of the car.
Oil has leaked out, or there are air bubbles inside the shock.
steps: Look for oil on the outside of each shock. Oil at the top means the cap or bladder (the rubber cup under the cap) is damaged; oil at the bottom means the O-rings (small rubber seals around the shaft) are worn.
Push down each corner of the car and let go. Left and right should come back up at the same speed.
Refill with thicker shock oil. Shock oil thickness is measured in cSt (centistokes); a bigger number means thicker. Go up about 50 to 100 cSt at a time.
When filling, pour the oil in slowly, move the shaft up and down gently a few times, then leave the shock standing for 5 to 10 minutes so air bubbles rise out before closing it.
If the car sits low even when standing still, it needs stiffer springs. Spring collars only raise the car; they don't make the spring stiffer.
warn: Never hold a shock shaft with bare pliers. Scratches on the shaft cause leaks. Wrap it in tape first or use shock pliers.
tip: Check the cSt number, not the 'wt' number. Different brands' 30wt oils can be very different thicknesses.
faq: Why do my shock caps keep popping off?

Usually the shock is overfilled with oil or has trapped air, so pressure builds on hard landings. Fill to just below the rim, let bubbles rise before closing, and bleed off the excess. Aluminium caps and a turn of Teflon tape on the threads help on bashers.
Why are my shocks leaking oil?
Oil at the top points to a damaged bladder or cap; oil at the bottom points to worn O-rings or a scratched shaft. Rebuild with fresh seals and check the shaft for scratches or bends.
What shock oil should I use for a crawler?

Crawlers usually run thicker oil than bashers, often in the 500–800 cSt range, so the chassis settles smoothly instead of bouncing. In Indian summer heat, going one step thicker keeps damping consistent.
Does tightening the spring collar make suspension stiffer?
No. Preload collars only raise ride height. To make the suspension stiffer you need stiffer springs or thicker oil.
cause: Usually shock oil that's too thin (worse in summer heat), springs too soft, or a leaking shock.
quick: Look for oil on the outside of each shock and fix the leak first.
Refill with thicker oil, 50–100 cSt higher at a time, and let the bubbles rise out.
If the car sags even when parked, fit stiffer springs. Collars only raise ride height.

title: Weak, slow or buzzing steering
summary: The wheels turn in the air but not on the ground, steering is slow, or the servo buzzes.
words: steering weak slow won't turn not turning wheels don't turn servo buzzing humming jitter shaking not centering pulls one side steering not straight servo saver dual rate
causes: The D/R (dual rate, a knob on the controller that limits how far the wheels turn) has been turned down.
Something in the steering is stiff, bent or rubbing.
The servo saver (a spring part that protects the servo from hits) is too soft and gives way.
The servo (the small motor that turns the wheels) is too weak for the tyres, or its gears are worn.
The BEC (the part that gives power to the servo, usually inside the speed controller) can't supply enough power for a big servo.
steps: Check the steering D/R knob on your controller is turned all the way up.
Take the servo horn (the arm on top of the servo) off the servo and move the front wheels by hand. They should swing side to side smoothly. If not, look for bent parts, dirt or tight screws.
Check the plugs: steering goes in channel 1 (CH1) on the receiver.
To centre it properly, switch on the controller and the car with the horn off, then fit the horn straight across.

Set the EPA (end point adjustment, how far the servo is allowed to turn each way) so the servo stops just before the wheels hit their limit. A servo that buzzes at full lock is pushing against a stop and will overheat.
If the steering still gives way on the ground, tighten the servo saver or fit a stronger servo. For a 1/10 crawler, look for at least 20 kg torque with metal gears.
warn: If your servo is rated for high voltage (HV), check the BEC voltage it gets. A servo rated at 7.4V loses roughly a fifth of its strength on 6V.
tip: A slow, sticky or shaky servo can also be worn inside. If it jitters even with the horn off, it's time for a new one.
faq: Why do my wheels turn in the air but not on the ground?
The servo is losing to tyre grip. Check dual rate first, then look for binding in the steering, a soft servo saver, or a servo that's simply too weak for the tyres.
Why does my servo buzz or get hot at full lock?
The endpoints are set past the steering's mechanical stops, so the servo keeps pushing against them. Reduce EPA on each side until the buzzing stops.
Why does my steering servo keep stripping?
Stock plastic-gear servos on small crawlers like the SCX24 and TRX-4M strip easily on rocks. A metal-gear servo with correctly set endpoints usually solves it for good.
Are cheap MG996R servos good for RC cars?
They're robotics servos, and many sold online are copies with plastic gears inside. For a 1/10 car, a waterproof 20–35 kg digital RC servo is far more reliable.
Plastic or aluminium servo horn?
Use a servo saver on fast bashers so impacts don't strip the servo. A rigid aluminium horn suits slow crawlers, but only with a metal-gear servo and properly set endpoints.
cause: Usually the dual rate (D/R) is turned down, something in the linkage binds, or the servo is too weak.
quick: Turn the steering D/R knob on your controller fully up.
Take the servo horn off and check the wheels swing freely by hand.
Set the end points (EPA) so the servo doesn't buzz at full lock.
Still weak on the ground? Fit a metal-gear servo, 20 kg or more for a 1/10 crawler.

title: Battery runs out too fast
summary: The car slows down or stops after only a few minutes.
words: battery dies fast quickly short run time runtime stops after few minutes cuts out cutoff slows down lipo nimh drains charge not lasting low voltage
causes: The battery is old. LiPo batteries (the usual flat rechargeable packs) wear out after a few hundred charges.
The LVC (low-voltage cutoff, a safety feature in the speed controller that stops the car when the battery gets low) is switching off early because the battery voltage drops under load.
Something is dragging, like a stiff bearing or gears that are too tight.
Dirty or loose battery plugs.
steps: Charge the battery fully and check each cell (each section inside the battery) with a cell checker. A full cell reads 4.20V, and all cells should read almost the same.
Spin each wheel by hand with the battery unplugged. They should spin freely. Gritty or stiff wheels mean the bearings (small metal rings the wheel spins on) need cleaning or replacing.
Clean the battery and speed controller plugs with isopropyl alcohol and a cotton bud.
Check the speed controller is set to the right battery type (LiPo or NiMH). The wrong setting can cut power early.
Charge with a balance charger at 1C (the battery's capacity in amps: a 2200 mAh battery charges at 2.2A).
warn: If a LiPo battery is puffed up (swollen), stop using it. Don't charge it, press it or puncture it. Never charge a LiPo when nobody is around. If one catches fire, use sand, not water.
tip: If you won't use a LiPo for more than a day or two, use the charger's storage mode to keep it at about 3.80 to 3.85V per cell. Stored full, it wears out much faster.
faq: Why does my RC car stop after a few minutes?
Usually the low-voltage cutoff is tripping because an ageing or low-C battery sags under load. Check each cell's voltage, spin the wheels for drag, and clean the plugs.
How long should an RC LiPo battery last?
Looked after properly and stored at storage voltage, a good pack lasts a few hundred charge cycles. Stored full or run flat, it can wear out in under a hundred.
Is my LiPo battery dead if it won't charge?
If the charger shows low voltage, a cell has dropped below about 3.0V. Packs discharged that far are not worth reviving; replace the battery.
Smart LiPo or regular LiPo?
Smart packs add convenience features but cost more and need matching chargers. A regular LiPo with a standard balance lead works with any balance charger and is usually the better value.
cause: Usually an ageing LiPo, the low-voltage cutoff tripping early, or drag in the drivetrain.
quick: Fully charge and check each cell: about 4.20V each, all close together.
Spin each wheel by hand. Anything gritty or stiff is wasting battery.
Make sure the ESC is set to the right battery type (LiPo or NiMH).
Stop using any battery that has puffed up.

title: Sliding, no grip or can't climb
summary: The wheels spin, the car slides around, or it can't get up rocks and slopes.
words: no grip sliding slipping spinning wheels spin traction can't climb slope rocks tyres slipping slides out spin out loose
causes: The tyre tread (the pattern on the tyre) or compound (how soft the rubber is) doesn't suit the surface.
Old, hard or dirty tyres.
The foam inserts (the sponge inside the tyre that holds its shape) are squashed or wet.
On crawlers, the weight is too high or too far back.
steps: Match the tread to where you drive: big blocks or lugs for dirt, mud and rocks; small pins for grass and turf; smooth slicks only for clean, flat ground.
Wash the tyres in warm soapy water and let them dry. Dust on the rubber kills grip.
Check the tyre is still glued to the rim all the way round.
Press the tyre. If it folds flat easily, the insert is worn and needs replacing.
For crawlers, add weight low down and towards the front, like brass (heavy metal) wheels, hubs or steering parts. It helps the car climb without tipping back.
tip: Softer tyres grip better on rocks but wear faster on rough ground and hot roads.
faq: Which tyres are best for rock crawling?
Soft compound tyres with deep lugs and soft foam or silicone inserts, so the tyre wraps around the rock. Add weight low and to the front for steeper climbs.
Why do my RC tyres balloon at high speed?
Non-belted tyres stretch outward at high RPM, which makes the car unstable. Belted tyres stop it; gearing down slightly also helps.
Should I vent my RC tyres?
Venting stops water and mud getting trapped inside. Seal the holes in the rim and make a few small holes in the centre of the tread instead, so spinning throws water out.
How do I glue RC tyres to the rim?
Clean the bead and rim with isopropyl alcohol, centre the insert, then run a thin line of CA tyre glue into the bead groove a section at a time, pressing firmly. Let it cure fully before driving.
cause: Usually the wrong tread or compound for the surface, dirty tyres, or worn foam inserts.
quick: Match the tread to the ground: lugs for dirt and rock, pins for grass.
Wash the tyres in warm soapy water. Dust kills grip.
Squeeze each tyre. If it folds flat easily, replace the insert.
On crawlers, add weight low and towards the front.

title: Car is too slow
summary: Top speed is lower than it should be, or the car feels lazy.
words: slow not fast enough top speed speed more speed power lacks power sluggish lazy faster acceleration punch
causes: A speed limit setting is switched on, on the controller or the speed controller.
The ESC (electronic speed controller, the box that controls the motor) hasn't been set up with your controller.
Something in the drivetrain (all the parts between motor and wheels) is dragging.
The gearing is set for climbing or control, not speed.
steps: Check your controller for a throttle limit switch or knob (often marked 50% / 75% / 100%) and set it to 100%.
Check the ESC isn't in a training or beginner mode. The manual shows how to switch modes.
Calibrate the ESC so it knows your controller's full throttle and brake. Usually you hold the set button, then show it neutral, full throttle and full brake, following the beeps in the manual.
Lift the car and spin the wheels by hand. They should turn easily.
For more speed, fit a pinion (the small gear on the motor) one or two teeth bigger. More teeth means more speed but more heat.
warn: After changing gearing, drive for 3 to 5 minutes and touch the motor. If you can't hold your finger on it for 3 seconds, it's too hot. Go back to the smaller pinion.
tip: The biggest speed jump is going from a brushed motor to a brushless one (a motor without brushes inside, which wastes far less power). Read 'Going brushless' under Upgrades first.
faq: How can I make my RC car faster?
First check for a throttle limit or training mode and calibrate the ESC. Then try a pinion one or two teeth bigger, watching temperatures. The big step up is a brushless motor and ESC.
How do I increase top speed on an SCX24?
Crawlers are geared for control, not speed. A faster motor or higher-speed gearing helps, but the worm or plastic gears may need upgrading to cope.
Does a bigger pinion make my car faster?
Yes, more teeth gives more top speed but less acceleration and more heat. Change one or two teeth at a time and check the motor temperature after each run.
cause: Usually a throttle limit left on, an ESC in training mode or not calibrated, or conservative gearing.
quick: Set the throttle limit on your controller to 100%.
Switch the ESC out of training mode and calibrate it to your controller.
Check the wheels spin freely by hand.
For more speed, go one or two teeth up on the pinion and watch motor heat.

title: Stuck on the trail
summary: Your crawler can't get over an obstacle, tips over on climbs, or the winch struggles.
words: stuck trail can't climb crawler rock tips over flips backward hill winch recovery pull rescue stall
causes: Weight sits too high or too far back, so the car tips on climbs.
Tyres or inserts are too hard to grip the rock.
A winch powered from the receiver doesn't get enough power under load.
steps: Drive slowly. Most crawler climbs are won with steady, low throttle.
Add weight low and to the front: brass wheels, hubs or steering cups.
Fit softer tyres or inserts so the tyre wraps around the rock.
For a heavy pull, double the winch line with a snatch block (a small pulley hooked to the car), which halves the load on the winch.
Power the winch straight from the battery or from a separate BEC, not only from the receiver.
If the winch stops and blinks, its overload protection has switched on. Let it cool for a few minutes.
tip: A cheap bumper winch looks great, but for real pulling a stronger winch with metal gears lasts much longer.
faq: Why does my crawler lift a front wheel when climbing?
That's torque twist: the driveshaft's reaction twists the chassis. Stiffer springs or thicker oil on the rear corner that compresses, and weight on the lifting wheel, reduce it.
Bumper winch or internal servo winch?
A bumper winch looks the part but small ones strip under heavy pulls. A servo winch mounted inside the chassis is much stronger for real recovery.
How do I add weight to my RC crawler?
Use brass wheels, hubs, steering cups or knuckles: low down and towards the front. Avoid weight high up on the body, which makes the car tip.
cause: Usually weight too high or too far back, tyres too hard for rock, or an underpowered winch.
quick: Drive slowly with steady, low throttle.
Add weight low and at the front: brass wheels, hubs or steering cups.
Fit softer tyres or inserts so the tyre wraps the rock.
Power the winch from the battery or its own BEC, not just the receiver.

title: Car not responding or glitching
summary: The car twitches, ignores the controller, loses signal at short range, or runs off on its own.
words: signal glitch glitching not responding no response lost signal range twitching runs away controller not working remote not working receiver bind pairing antenna dropouts failsafe
causes: Weak batteries in the controller.
The receiver antenna (the thin wire coming out of the receiver) is cut, kinked or sitting against metal.
The receiver sits right next to the motor, speed controller or battery wires.
A big servo pulls so much power that the receiver resets for a moment.
steps: Put fresh batteries in the controller.
Check the antenna wire isn't cut or bent sharply. Run it up through a plastic antenna tube so the tip stands straight up, away from metal and carbon fibre.
Move the receiver as far as you can from the motor, speed controller and thick battery wires.
Check every plug is pushed fully into the receiver: steering in CH1, speed controller in CH2.
Re-bind (pair) the controller and receiver again, following the manual.
Test the failsafe (what the car does when it loses signal): with the wheels off the ground, switch off the controller. The car should stop, not keep driving.
warn: Controllers and receivers from different brands, or even different systems from the same brand, usually can't pair. Check they match before buying.
tip: If the glitches happen when you steer hard, the servo is draining the power. A separate BEC fixes it.
faq: Why is my RC car not responding to the controller?
Check controller batteries, then that the receiver is bound and plugs are fully seated (steering CH1, ESC CH2). If it worked before, re-bind it.
Why does my RC car glitch when I steer?
A strong servo can pull the receiver's voltage down for a moment. A separate BEC or a capacitor (glitch buster) on a spare receiver port fixes it.
Can I use a different brand controller with my receiver?
Usually not. Even within one brand, different protocols don't bind. Buy the controller and receiver as a matching set.
cause: Usually weak controller batteries, a damaged or badly placed antenna, or a receiver too close to power wiring.
quick: Put fresh batteries in the controller.
Run the antenna wire straight up in a tube, away from metal and carbon.
Move the receiver away from the motor, ESC and battery wires.
Re-bind, then test that the car stops when you switch the controller off.

title: Lights dim, flickering or not working
summary: New lights won't switch on, glow weakly, or flicker while driving.
words: lights not working dim flicker flickering led headlight light bar night spotlight lamp roof light dark
causes: The light needs more voltage than the receiver gives. Receiver ports give about 5 to 6V; many light bars need 12V.
The LEDs are connected the wrong way round.
A plug is loose or only half pushed in.
Too many lights on the receiver, so they dim when the servo works.
steps: Check the voltage on the light's label or listing. 12V lights need power straight from the battery (a 3S LiPo) or from a 12V BEC, not from the receiver.
Check LED direction: the longer leg is plus (+); the flat edge on the LED is minus (−).
Connect several LEDs side by side (in parallel), not one after another.
Push every plug in fully and check none of the little pins have backed out.
If lights flicker when you steer, they share power with the servo. Give them their own power supply.
warn: Never connect a bare LED straight to a battery without the right resistor. It burns out instantly.
tip: A light controller lets you switch lights from your transmitter and keeps the wiring neat when you take the body off.
faq: Why are my RC LED lights so dim?
They likely need 12V but are running off the receiver's 5–6V. Power 12V lights from the battery (3S) or a 12V BEC.
Why do my RC lights flicker?
Loose receiver pins, or a BEC that sags when the servo works. Seat every plug fully and give the lights their own power supply.
cause: Usually 12V lights on a 5–6V receiver port, LEDs wired the wrong way round, or loose plugs.
quick: Check the light's voltage. 12V lights need battery power or a 12V BEC.
Check LED direction: long leg is plus (+), flat edge is minus (−).
If they flicker when you steer, give them their own power supply.

title: Speed controller blinking or car won't move
summary: The ESC flashes or beeps, the motor stops, or the car has no power at all.
words: esc blinking flashing beeping red light green light won't move car not moving no power motor not working motor stopped cuts out thermal shutdown calibrate
causes: The battery is flat, or the low-voltage cutoff has switched on.
The ESC (electronic speed controller) or motor got too hot and paused to protect itself.
The ESC isn't calibrated to your controller, or the throttle trim isn't at zero.
A loose motor or battery wire.
steps: Most blinking is a safety message, not damage. Look up the blink pattern in your ESC's manual first.
Charge the battery and check the ESC is set to the right battery type.
If the motor or ESC is very hot, let them cool by themselves. Don't put them in a fridge or freezer.
Set the throttle trim knob on the controller back to zero.
Calibrate the ESC again following its manual.
Check the three motor wires and the battery plug are pushed in fully and not burnt.
warn: If it keeps overheating, fit a smaller pinion and check nothing is dragging. Running hot again and again will damage the motor and ESC.
tip: A program card lets you change ESC settings like cutoff voltage and brake strength without counting beeps.
faq: Why is my ESC blinking red?
On most ESCs a blinking red light means low voltage or overheating. Charge the battery, let everything cool, and check the manual for that exact pattern.
Why is my ESC blinking red and green?
Commonly a battery-type mismatch or voltage protection: for example LiPo cutoff selected with a NiMH pack, or too many cells. Check the battery setting and your ESC's maximum voltage.
How do I calibrate my ESC?
Most ESCs: hold the set button while switching on, then show it neutral, full throttle and full brake as the beeps or lights prompt. Follow your ESC's manual for the exact sequence.
cause: Usually a safety mode: flat battery, low-voltage cutoff, overheating or calibration.
quick: Look up the blink pattern in your ESC's manual first. Most blinking isn't damage.
Charge the battery and check the ESC's battery-type setting.
Let a hot motor or ESC cool naturally, then set throttle trim back to zero.
Recalibrate the ESC and check every motor and battery wire is pushed fully in.

title: Motor or ESC getting too hot
summary: The motor is too hot to touch, or the car keeps cutting out after a few minutes.
words: hot overheating overheat motor hot esc hot too hot thermal heat shuts down summer temperature burning smell
causes: The pinion is too big for the motor, battery or tyres.
Something is dragging: tight gears, dirty bearings, grass wrapped around an axle.
Hot weather. In 40°C summers there is very little room before parts overheat.
Bigger, heavier tyres than stock, which work like a bigger pinion.
steps: Drive 3 to 5 minutes, stop, and touch the motor. If you can't keep your finger on it for 3 seconds (about 75°C), it's too hot.
Fit a pinion one or two teeth smaller and test again.
Spin the wheels by hand to check nothing drags, and pull out any grass or string around the axles.
Fit a motor cooling fan and keep the fins clean.
In summer, drive early morning or in the evening, and rest the car between batteries.
warn: Don't check temperature right after driving through water. The water cools the outside and hides the heat.
tip: Keep LiPo batteries in a cool room indoors, never in a parked car or a sunny shed.
faq: How hot is too hot for an RC motor?
If you can't keep a finger on it for about 3 seconds, it's too hot. Gear down a tooth or two and check for drag.
Why does my RC car cut out when it gets hot?
The ESC's thermal protection is pausing power to protect the electronics. Let it cool naturally, then fit a smaller pinion or add a fan.
cause: Usually a pinion too large for the setup, drag in the drivetrain, or summer heat.
quick: After 3–5 minutes, touch the motor. If you can't hold it for 3 seconds, it's too hot.
Fit a pinion one or two teeth smaller.
Clear anything dragging, like tight gears or grass around the axles.
Add a cooling fan and drive in the cooler hours.

title: Wheel wobbling or coming off
summary: A wheel shakes, sits crooked, or the wheel nut keeps coming loose.
words: wheel wobble wobbling shaking wheel loose falls off wheel nut hex stripped crooked bent axle tyre came off rim
causes: A loose wheel nut.
A worn or stripped wheel hex (the six-sided adapter between the axle and the wheel).
A bent axle or driveshaft.
Wet foam inside the tyre, which makes it heavy on one side.
steps: Tighten the wheel nut until it's snug. Too tight can stop the wheel turning freely.
Take the wheel off and check the hex and its small drive pin. Rounded corners mean it needs replacing.
Roll the axle on a flat table. If it wobbles as it rolls, it's bent.
Squeeze the tyre. If water comes out, let it dry fully before driving again.
tip: A nut with a nylon ring inside (a lock nut) won't shake loose as easily.
faq: How do I fix a stripped wheel hex?
Replace the hex if it's metal and rounded. If the hex socket in a plastic wheel is worn, the wheel itself needs replacing; metal hexes with a clamping nut last much longer.
Why does my RC car wobble at high speed?
Common causes are a waterlogged tyre foam, an unglued tyre, a bent axle or a loose wheel nut. Check each wheel by spinning it and watching for a wobble.
cause: Usually a loose wheel nut, a rounded wheel hex, or a bent axle.
quick: Tighten the wheel nut until snug, not so tight the wheel binds.
Check the hex and drive pin. Rounded corners mean replace it.
Roll the axle on a flat table. A wobble means it's bent.

title: Driveshaft popping out or clicking
summary: A driveshaft falls out, or the car clicks or jerks when turning or climbing.
words: driveshaft drive shaft popping out falls out dogbone cvd clicking jerking lurching turning full lock universal joint
causes: The driveshaft is too short or the suspension drops too far, so it slips out.
The joints at each end of a driveshaft aren't lined up, which makes the car jerk at low speed.
Worn plastic driveshafts or cups.
steps: With the battery out, turn the steering to full lock and let the suspension hang down. Check the driveshaft still sits fully in its cups.
Line up both end joints of each driveshaft so they face the same way. This is called phasing and stops low-speed jerks.
Replace plastic driveshafts with metal ones, especially after a motor upgrade.
tip: Metal driveshafts should match your car model exactly. Lengths differ even between similar trucks.
faq: Why does my dogbone keep falling out?
The suspension droops further than the dogbone can reach, or the cups are worn. Limit droop slightly, or switch to longer driveshafts or CVDs that stay engaged.
Why does my crawler jerk at low speed?
The driveshaft joints are out of phase. Set both U-joint yokes on each shaft to face the same direction.
cause: Usually a driveshaft too short for the suspension travel, joints out of phase, or worn plastic shafts.
quick: At full lock with the suspension hanging down, check the shaft stays in its cups.
Line up both end joints so they face the same way (phasing).
Swap worn plastic shafts for metal ones, especially after a motor upgrade.

title: Body shell cracking or paint peeling
summary: The polycarbonate body splits at the corners or mounting holes, or the paint flakes off.
words: body shell cracked cracking split broken lexan polycarbonate paint peeling flaking body post holes repair reinforce
causes: Thin polycarbonate (Lexan) splits at corners and body-post holes after repeated impacts, especially in cold weather.
Paint flakes when the shell wasn't washed before painting, or when the wrong paint type was used.
steps: Wash the inside of the shell with warm soapy water to remove mould-release oil before any repair or paint.
Reinforce high-stress areas from the inside with self-adhesive fibreglass mesh tape, then a thin layer of flexible shoe-repair adhesive over it.
Stitch existing cracks with small zip ties through drilled holes, then cover with the same adhesive.
Paint only with polycarbonate paint, sprayed on the inside of the shell, darkest colours first.
Let paint cure 24–48 hours before adding decals or reinforcement.
warn: Ordinary hobby or acrylic paint isn't flexible enough for a polycarbonate shell and will crack off at the first impact.
tip: Reinforce a new body before its first run. It's far easier than repairing it later.
faq: How do I stop my RC body from cracking?
Reinforce the inside with fibreglass mesh tape and a flexible adhesive at the corners and post holes, before the first run.
Why is the paint peeling off my RC body?
Either the mould-release oil wasn't washed off, or non-polycarbonate paint was used. Polycarbonate paint, sprayed inside the shell, flexes with it.
cause: Usually repeated impacts splitting thin polycarbonate at corners and post holes, or the wrong paint.
quick: Wash the inside of the shell before any repair or paint.
Reinforce stress points from inside with fibreglass mesh tape and flexible glue.
Paint only with polycarbonate paint, on the inside of the shell.

title: Your first upgrades, in the right order
summary: What's worth upgrading first, so your money makes the car better and more reliable.
words: first upgrade upgrades beginner start what to buy new car starter where to start best upgrade order
steps: A good balance charger and a spare battery. More driving time and safer charging come first.
Good hex drivers (screwdrivers with six-sided tips). Cheap ones round off screws.
Tyres that suit where you drive. This changes how the car feels more than anything else.
A stronger metal-gear servo, so the steering keeps up with the new tyres.
Sealed bearings, if your car came with plastic bushings (simple sleeves instead of bearings).
Then drive it until something breaks, and upgrade that part. Your car will show you its own weak spots.
tip: Before upgrading the motor, make the drivetrain stronger. More power just breaks weak gears faster.
faq: What is the first upgrade for a new RC car?
A good balance charger and spare battery, followed by tyres for your terrain and a stronger metal-gear servo. They improve every run before you spend on power.
What tools do I need for RC cars?
Quality hex drivers in 1.5, 2.0 and 2.5 mm, nut drivers in 5.5 and 7 mm, blue threadlock, shock pliers and a cell checker cover most jobs. Cheap hex keys round off screws.
Which RC parts break most often?
Typically spur gears, servo gears, driveshafts, suspension arms and wheel hexes. It's worth keeping a spare of whatever your model is known to break.
quick: A balance charger and a spare battery.
Proper hex drivers, so screws don't round off.
Tyres that suit your ground, then a metal-gear servo to turn them.
After that, upgrade whatever breaks first.

title: Going brushless
summary: How to move from a brushed to a brushless motor without breaking the rest of the car.
words: brushless upgrade brushed to brushless motor esc combo kv more power faster 2s 3s conversion
steps: Buy a matched brushless combo (motor and ESC sold together), so they work together out of the box.
Choose the KV (how fast the motor spins per volt) for your battery. Higher voltage needs a lower KV, or the motor will overheat.
Before fitting it, strengthen the drivetrain: metal gears and metal driveshafts.
Start on 2S (a 2-cell LiPo battery). Only move to 3S once the car survives 2S without breaking.
When you go up in battery cells, fit a pinion one or two teeth smaller.
Check the motor temperature after every few runs until you know the setup is safe.
warn: Check your car's maximum battery rating before going to 3S or higher. Many small cars are only built for 2S.
tip: Brushless motors waste much less power as heat, so you usually get more speed and longer run time from the same battery.
faq: Is brushless worth it for a beginner?
Yes, once the car is reliable. It gives more speed, cooler running and longer run time. Strengthen the drivetrain first and start on 2S.
What KV motor should I choose?
Lower KV for higher voltage and heavier cars, higher KV for 2S and lighter cars. A matched motor and ESC combo takes the guesswork out.
quick: Buy a matched motor and ESC combo.
Pick a lower KV for higher-voltage batteries.
Strengthen the drivetrain first: metal gears and driveshafts.
Start on 2S, and drop a pinion tooth or two when you add cells.

title: Metal or plastic? Where metal actually helps
summary: More metal isn't always better. Here's where it helps and where plastic is the smarter choice.
words: metal aluminium aluminum plastic upgrade alloy cnc which parts metal vs plastic stronger durable
steps: Keep suspension arms and bumpers plastic. Good plastic bends and springs back in a crash; metal bends for good and passes the hit on to more expensive parts.
Go metal for parts that must stay stiff and exact: steering knuckles, shock towers, motor mounts, servo horns and shock caps.
On crawlers, metal or brass parts low down also add useful weight.
Skip cheap 'full metal' upgrade kits. They make the car heavier and often less reliable.
tip: A cheap plastic part that breaks is often protecting a more expensive part behind it.
faq: Are aluminium suspension arms better than plastic?
Not for bashing or racing. Plastic arms flex and return, and protect the bulkheads behind them; aluminium arms bend permanently and pass the impact on.
Which parts are worth upgrading to metal?
Shock caps and bodies, motor mounts, servo horns, steering knuckles and C-hubs, and diff cases. Keep arms and bumpers plastic.
quick: Keep arms and bumpers plastic. They flex and protect costlier parts.
Go metal where parts must stay stiff: knuckles, towers, motor mounts, servo horns.
Skip cheap 'full metal' kits. They add weight, not reliability.

title: Better crawling
summary: Upgrades that make a scale crawler climb better, in the order that helps most.
words: crawler crawling better climbing scale trail rock upgrades scx24 scx10 trx4 fcx crawl
steps: Soft tyres with good inserts. This is the single biggest improvement.
Weight low and at the front: brass wheels, hubs or steering cups.
A strong, metal-gear steering servo, so the wheels turn even when pressed into rocks.
Slightly thicker shock oil, so the car settles smoothly instead of bouncing.
A motor and ESC with good low-speed control and drag brake (holds the car still on slopes when you let go of the throttle).
tip: Practice slow, steady throttle. Driving style matters as much as parts on the rocks.
faq: What should I upgrade first on an SCX24?
A metal-gear servo, sticky tyres and a little brass weight low at the front. Then steel worm gears if you upgrade the motor.
What are the common TRX-4M problems?
Owners often report drag from plastic bushings, a weak stock servo and plastic diff gears. A sealed bearing kit is usually the first fix, then a metal-gear servo.
quick: Soft tyres with good inserts: the biggest single gain.
Weight low and at the front.
A strong metal-gear steering servo.
A motor and ESC with smooth low-speed control and drag brake.

title: Which gear fits my car?
summary: How to read pitch, tooth count and shaft size before buying a pinion or spur gear.
words: which gear fits pitch module mod 0.8 32p 48p 64p mod1 pinion size teeth tooth count shaft bore 3.175 5mm gear compatibility
steps: Find the pitch (tooth size) of your spur gear. It's usually printed on the gear or in the manual: 48P, 32P, Mod 0.8 and Mod 1 are the common ones.
Buy a pinion with the same pitch. 32P and Mod 0.8 look almost the same but are not the same.
Check the bore (the hole for the motor shaft): 3.175 mm (1/8 inch) on most 1/10 motors, 5 mm on bigger ones.
Count the teeth. More teeth on the pinion means more speed and more heat; fewer means more climbing power and cooler running.
Change one or two teeth at a time, and check the motor temperature after each change.
warn: Copying someone else's tooth count only works if they have the same car. Different gearboxes change the final result.
tip: Roughly: 48P for 1/10 buggies and touring cars, 32P or Mod 0.8 for 1/10 trucks and crawlers, Mod 1 for 1/8 and heavy trucks.
faq: How do I know which pinion fits my car?
Match the pitch printed on your spur gear (for example 48P, 32P, Mod 0.8 or Mod 1) and the motor shaft size, usually 3.175 mm or 5 mm.
What does 32P or Mod 0.8 mean?
Both describe tooth size. 'P' (pitch) counts teeth per inch, 'Mod' measures tooth size in millimetres. They're close but not interchangeable.
quick: Find your spur gear's pitch (48P, 32P, Mod 0.8, Mod 1) and match it exactly.
Check the bore: 3.175 mm on most 1/10 motors, 5 mm on bigger ones.
More pinion teeth means more speed and heat. Change one or two at a time.

title: 5-minute check after every run
summary: A quick routine that prevents most breakdowns.
words: maintenance after run check routine care cleaning service regular checklist prevent
steps: Unplug the battery straight away.
Brush dirt off the motor and speed controller so they can cool.
Spin each wheel by hand and listen for grinding bearings.
Check the screws that shake loose most: servo horn, steering links, lower shock screws, suspension pins and wheel nuts.
Every 5 runs, check gear mesh, driveshafts, tyre glue and steering endpoints.
Every 10 to 15 batteries, or after mud or water, clean and oil the bearings and check the shocks.
tip: Store the car on a stand so the tyres don't get flat spots.
faq: How often should I service my RC car?
A quick check after every run, a closer look every five runs, and bearings and shocks every 10–15 batteries or after any wet or muddy run.
How do I clean RC car bearings?
Soak them in cleaner, spin them dry, then add a drop of light bearing oil. Replace any that still feel gritty.
quick: Unplug the battery and brush dirt off the motor and ESC.
Spin each wheel and listen for grinding bearings.
Check the screws that shake loose: servo horn, links, shock screws, wheel nuts.

title: Driving in Indian summer heat
summary: At 40°C and above, parts overheat much sooner. Simple changes keep the car running.
words: summer heat hot weather temperature india 40 degrees overheating sun afternoon
steps: Drive early in the morning or in the evening, not in the afternoon sun.
Fit a pinion one or two teeth smaller than in winter.
Add a cooling fan to the motor and keep air flowing through the body.
Use slightly thicker shock oil, because heat thins it.
Rest the car between batteries and let the motor cool.
Keep LiPo batteries indoors in a cool room. Never leave them in a parked car or in the sun.
warn: Don't charge a LiPo that is still hot from driving. Let it cool down first.
faq: Is it okay to run my RC car in 40°C heat?
Yes, with care: gear down a tooth or two, add a motor fan, run in the morning or evening, and let things cool between packs.
quick: Drive early morning or evening.
Run a pinion one or two teeth smaller than in winter, and add a cooling fan.
Use slightly thicker shock oil.
Keep LiPos indoors and never charge one that's still hot.

title: Dust and monsoon care
summary: Fine dust and wet weather wear out bearings and rust metal parts fast. Here's what to do.
words: dust dirt mud water wet rain monsoon rust corrosion waterproof cleaning washing after rain
steps: Use rubber-sealed bearings (marked 2RS) instead of metal-shielded ones. They keep fine dust out much longer.
Keep the gear cover on and closed.
Brush dust off with a soft brush. Don't blow hard with compressed air; it pushes grit into the bearings.
After a wet run, unplug the battery, spin the water out of the tyres, and wipe or rinse off mud gently. Never use a pressure washer.
Dry the car, then spray a little water-displacing spray on screws, pins and drive cups and wipe off the extra.
Open the receiver box and let it air-dry for a few hours. Never close a damp car in a bag.
warn: 'Waterproof' electronics don't stop bearings, screws and foams from rusting or rotting. They still need drying after every wet run.
faq: Can I drive my RC car in the rain?
Only if the electronics are waterproof, and even then bearings, screws and foams still need drying and oiling afterwards. Never close up a damp car.
How do I stop my RC car rusting?
Dry it fully after wet runs and spray a little water-displacing oil on screws, pins and drive cups, wiping off the excess.
quick: Fit rubber-sealed (2RS) bearings and keep the gear cover on.
Brush dust off. Don't blast it with compressed air.
After a wet run, dry everything and spray screws and pins with water-displacing spray.

title: LiPo battery safety and storage
summary: How to charge, store and get rid of LiPo batteries safely so they last longer.
words: lipo battery safety storage charging puffed swollen fire storage voltage balance charge dispose old battery
steps: Always use a balance charger (a charger that fills each cell evenly) on the LiPo setting.
Charge at 1C: a 2200 mAh battery at 2.2A, a 5000 mAh battery at 5A.
Never charge when nobody is around, and never charge on a bed, sofa or carpet.
If you won't use it for more than a day or two, use storage mode (about 3.80 to 3.85V per cell).
Never run a cell below 3.0V. Set the speed controller's cutoff to LiPo.
Keep batteries in a fireproof LiPo bag or a metal box, in a cool room.
warn: A puffed (swollen) battery should never be charged, pressed or punctured. Tape the plug, keep it away from anything that burns, and take it to an e-waste or battery collection point.
tip: A LiPo kept at storage voltage lasts hundreds of charges. One stored full or run flat often lasts under a hundred.
faq: What should I do with a puffed LiPo battery?
Stop using it. Don't charge, press or puncture it; tape the plug and take it to an e-waste or battery collection point.
What voltage should I store a LiPo at?
About 3.80–3.85V per cell. Most balance chargers have a storage mode that does this automatically.
Is my cheap balance charger genuine?
Copies of popular chargers are common and some overcharge or lack proper cooling. Buy from a trusted seller and check the maker's authenticity code where offered.
quick: Charge on a balance charger at 1C, never unattended.
Use storage mode (about 3.8V per cell) if you won't run it for a few days.
Never run a cell below 3.0V. Set the ESC cutoff to LiPo.
Retire any puffed battery safely.
